what_this_is: Materials the LIVE shell samples, as distinct from art/visual-study/, which holds the study's specimens and their retained captures. A file here is shipped and drawn every frame; a file there is evidence of a comparison that has already been made.

sources.author: Dimitrios Savva (photography), Rob Tuytel (processing)

files.encoding: OpenGL normal map -- +Y is up. Godot's convention is the same, so no channel is flipped on import.

sources.provenance: Byte-identical to the files the fidelity pilot downloaded and recorded in art/visual-study/fidelity-1/research.json. Copied rather than re-downloaded, and the hashes above were re-taken from the copies.

measured.brick_assumed: 215 mm stretcher + 10 mm perpend = 0.225 m; 65 mm brick + 10 mm bed = 0.075 m
measured.gives: 5 x 0.225 = 1.125 m wide, 15 x 0.075 = 1.125 m tall -- square in the world as well as in pixels, so one number scales both axes without stretching a brick
measured.how: ffmpeg -i brick-wall-diffuse.jpg -vf 'crop=2048:256:0:900,scale=1400:175' strip-h.png for the stretchers; crop=256:2048:900:0 for the courses. Count the joints.

scale.not_the_catalogue: Poly Haven states 3 m for this asset. That is the size of the WALL that was photographed, not a size this game has to adopt -- read as an instruction it gives bricks the size of a door.
scale.not_the_pilot: The fidelity round used 1.2. It counted the five stretchers correctly and then rounded; the 6% it lost is the difference between a 225 mm brick and a 240 mm one.
scale.warning: This is the size a real brick is, NOT a size anybody preferred. plans/0063's brick-scale round compared three apparent sizes against these same maps and the player selected none. Turn this dial when that round is settled.

mean.space: linear, NOT sRGB. The same image averages (0.396, 0.290, 0.239) as stored.
mean.why: The shader divides the sample by this to leave a ratio, so that the photograph supplies the grain and the Building's own paint supplies the colour. masonry_albedo is declared source_color and is therefore decoded before the division, so the stored average is the wrong number by the whole transfer curve.
mean.retake_it_with: ffmpeg -v error -i src/Borough.Godot/assets/city/brick-wall-diffuse.jpg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 - | python3 -c "import sys; raw=sys.stdin.buffer.read(); lin=lambda v:(v/255.0)/12.92 if v/255.0<=0.04045 else (((v/255.0)+0.055)/1.055)**2.4; lut=[lin(i) for i in range(256)]; print([sum(lut[v]*raw[c::3].count(v) for v in range(256))/len(raw[c::3]) for c in range(3)])"
mean.warning: Replacing the diffuse image means retaking this number. Nothing checks that they agree.

not_yet_used.standing: Asphalt012 is imported under art/visual-study/neighbourhood-1/ for the study's paving. The live roads still use surfaces.gdshader and sample no texture.
